content_of_post_to_comment:
For years I convinced myself that I had zero willpower. I thought discipline was some genetic gift handed out at birth that I simply did not possess. Whenever I tried to build good habits, I operated in complete binary mode. Either my day was flawless, or it was complete garbage.

If I woke up on time, hit the gym, and ate clean, I felt like a machine.

like a couple of weeks ago my alarm failed to go off and I woke up forty-five minutes late. I missed my morning workout window. An ordinary, disciplined adult would just shower, go to work, and do a quick thirty-minute jog in the evening. My brain did not do that. My brain immediately decided that the entire day was RUINED.

Because the morning was off-schedule, I decided the day was contaminated. I skipped my meal prep and ordered greasy fast food for lunch. I sat on my sofa scrolling short-form videos for four hours after work because "I will just reset on Monday."

Do you know how insane that logic is? It is literally the equivalent of getting one flat tire on the highway, pulling over to the shoulder, and deciding to slash the other three tires with a hunting knife. You turn a ten-minute inconvenience into a twelve-hour downward spiral. its not a lack of willpower, it is just self-sabotage dressed up as high standards. i should of figured out that a sixty percent day is still infinitely better than zero. Why do we treat personal habits like an all-or-nothing cult?
